meta.title: How to activate and stick your birlinq QR
meta.description: Step-by-step guide: how to activate a birlinq Move sticker and place it correctly on your windshield.

hero.title: Activate and install your birlinq Move sticker
hero.lead: Five minutes, and the sticker on your windshield starts working: whoever scans it sees a contact form, not your phone number.

activate.heading: How to activate
activate.lead: If the sticker isn't linked to your car yet, start here.
activate.s1Title: Scan the QR or enter the code
activate.s1Text: With your phone's camera — the link opens activation automatically. Or enter the sticker code and activation code from the back of the sticker manually.
activate.s2Title: Log in or create an account
activate.s2Text: A phone number or email is the only way to get notified when someone scans your QR.
activate.s3Text: Make, model, color. License plate is optional and hidden from strangers by default.
activate.s4Text: Choose what a scanner sees — from "vehicle type only" to an open profile with WhatsApp.
activate.s5Text: Done — the QR starts working right away.

place.heading: Where and how to place it
place.lead: This determines whether someone who wants to reach you can actually see the sticker.
place.whereText: Bottom-left corner of the windshield, outside or inside — as long as the QR is visible from the street.
place.prepText: Wipe the glass dry, peel the protective film off the sticker, and press for 20–30 seconds without air bubbles.
place.waitText: Avoid washing the car or touching the sticker for the first 24 hours.

check.heading: Check that it works
check.text: Scan your own sticker with another phone's camera and go through one scenario — make sure the notification arrives.

faq.heading: Frequently asked questions
faq.q1: The QR won't scan, or the code isn't found
faq.a1: Double-check the code for typos — 0/O and 1/I are easy to mix up. If the sticker is new, try scanning the QR again instead of entering it manually.
faq.q2: It says the sticker is already activated
faq.a2: If it's your sticker, log in to your dashboard — it's already linked to your account.
faq.q3: I want to change what a scanner can see
faq.a3: You can do that any time, in your dashboard's QR privacy settings.
faq.q4: The sticker came off or got damaged
faq.a4: You can activate a new sticker the same way as the first one. Pause the old one in "My QR codes".

push.heading: Notifications on your phone
push.lead: So you hear about a scan straight away, not from an email.
push.iosLead: Add birlinq to your Home Screen once and enable notifications from there. Works on iOS 16.4 and newer.
push.iosStep1: Open birlinq in Safari. If the link opened inside Telegram, WhatsApp or Instagram, tap “Open in Safari” there
push.iosStep2: Tap the Share button at the bottom of the screen:
push.iosStep3: Scroll the list down and choose “Add to Home Screen”:
push.iosStep4: Tap “Add” — a birlinq icon appears on your Home Screen
push.iosStep5: Open birlinq from that icon and sign in again: the Home Screen app has its own storage, so a Safari sign-in does not carry over
push.iosStep6: Tap “Enable notifications” and allow them in the iPhone prompt
push.iosNote: This is Apple's restriction: a normal Safari tab has no notifications at all, which is why no button appears there. Already added the icon? Then just open birlinq from it.
push.androidLead: Nothing to install — works in Chrome and Samsung Internet.
push.androidStep1: Open birlinq in your browser (not inside Telegram or WhatsApp), sign in to the cabinet and tap “Enable notifications”
push.androidStep2: Allow notifications in the prompt — on recent Android the system itself shows it
push.androidNote: If no prompt appeared, tap the lock icon left of the address, open Permissions and turn Notifications on.
push.androidSamsungNote: Samsung may put the browser to sleep to save battery, which delays notifications. Settings → Battery → Sleeping apps — remove the browser from the list.
